Save a reusable NIS cohort

Source: R/write-cohort.R
nis_write_cohort.Rd

Write cohort discharges and one zero-domain placeholder for each sampled hospital-year without a cohort discharge. Open the resulting directory with nis_open() and omit cohort in nis_design(). To narrow the cohort, filter the resulting survey design so its sampled hospitals stay in scope.

Usage

nis_write_cohort(.data, cohort, path, keep)

Arguments

.data

A lazy query from nis_open(), with any cohort flags added. Include the whole sample for the years you intend to analyze.

cohort

Logical data-masked cohort expression. Missing values are outside the cohort. Omit when re-saving a dataset written by this function.

path

A new output directory in an existing parent directory.

keep

Tidyselect expression or character vector of analysis columns to write. Rename columns on the query before exporting. YEAR, HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, and DISCWT are always written.

Value

The original path, invisibly. If collecting raw rows directly from the saved dataset, filter on .in_cohort to count only discharges.

Details

The output is a directory of yearly Zstandard-compressed Parquet parts. Each part records the cohort expression, the years opened by the source query, and the easyNIS version in its Parquet metadata. The expression is recorded as supplied, so also retain the code that defines any flags or variables it uses. The release check exempts the extract from comparison against HCUP release totals.

See also

nis_design(), Defining cohorts.

Examples

query <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp2QuqHF/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp2QuqHF/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
path <- nis_write_cohort(query, AGE >= 65, tempfile(), keep = LOS)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp2QuqHF/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(nis_open(path), keep = LOS)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmp2QuqHF/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
dplyr::summarise(design, discharges = srvyr::survey_total())
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   discharges discharges_se
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1       52.5          3.28
